title: Spalled 20-micron device films reuse each Czochralski donor fifteen times
idea: First principles: a DRAM die's devices live in the top <1 um of a 775 um wafer, so >99.8% of the high-purity silicon (and the quartz-crucible life that grew it) is mechanical ballast. Grow a 20 um epi layer, peel it off with a Ni-stressor controlled spall, bond it to a low-grade recycled handle wafer, then CMP and re-epi the donor for ~15 reuse cycles.
why: Cuts high-purity-quartz crucible and polysilicon intensity per wafer start ~10x (Spruce Pine chokepoint) and CZ energy per bit ~10x; the added bond/CMP cost per wafer is the trade.

title: Cold-crucible skull melting grows CZ ingots without any quartz
idea: A crucible's only job is to hold 1414 C silicon without contaminating it, and the purest container for silicon is solid silicon. Use a segmented water-cooled copper crucible with induction heating so a frozen Si skull lines the wall, and pull 300 mm crystals from an electromagnetically confined melt.
why: Eliminates high-purity quartz crucibles (>80% Spruce Pine) and crucible-sourced oxygen that seeds junction-leakage defects; costs ~30-50% more melt energy lost to cooling water.

title: Waste silicon tetrachloride becomes synthetic-silica crucibles beside polysilicon plants
idea: Crucible purity is set by metal content, not geology: Siemens polysilicon plants co-produce ~10-20 kg SiCl4 per kg Si, which flame hydrolysis (SiCl4 + 2H2 + O2 -> SiO2 + 4HCl, HCl recycled) turns into ppb-metal synthetic silica grain. Arc-fuse crucibles from it with a Ba-devitrified crystalline outer shell for 1450 C creep strength.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine HPQ dependence using a US waste stream next to existing polysilicon plants; synthetic grain is ~10x purer than natural HPQ.

title: Microgram hydrogen backside gas replaces helium in every wafer chuck
idea: Kinetic theory: free-molecular gas-gap conductance scales ~P/sqrt(m), so H2 (m=2) moves ~1.4x more heat per Torr than He (m=4). An on-tool PEM electrolyzer feeds 5-10 Torr H2 into the ~1 cm3 chuck backside volume (~2 ug inventory, orders below any ignition hazard), with interlocked N2 purge.
why: Chuck backside cooling is a dominant fab helium use and Qatar (~30% of supply) has been offline since March 2026; removes He from etch/CVD chucks at near-zero consumable cost.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek solid-contact chuck conducts heat with zero backside gas
idea: Contact conductance h ~ 1.25 k_s (m/sigma)(P/H)^0.95 grows with true contact area; a Johnsen-Rahbek chuck gives ~10x the clamp pressure of a Coulomb chuck, and a compliant 50 um pyrolytic-graphite skin raises true contact from ~0.1% to a few percent, reaching gas-gap-class 500-1000 W/m2K with no gas.
why: Removes helium entirely from chucks, including cryogenic etch where He cooling is critical; backside particle and carbon contamination control is the risk.

title: Nickel-aluminide intermetallic buried wordlines replace tungsten below 15 nanometers
idea: At sub-15 nm widths line resistivity scales with rho0*lambda (bulk resistivity x electron mean free path), not rho0, and ordered B2 NiAl has a few-nm mean free path so its size penalty is small. Fill buried-wordline trenches with Ni/Al ALD nanolaminates and anneal to NiAl, which self-passivates with Al2O3 and needs no TiN barrier.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry from DRAM's largest W use; barrier-free fill gives ~20-30% more conductor cross-section and lower wordline RC.

title: Tin-oxide rutile template grows k~90 TiO2 capacitors without Ru
idea: Rutile TiO2 has k~90-170 but only forms rutile at DRAM temperatures on a rutile-structured template, today RuO2 (Ru ~90% South Africa). Use conductive Sb:SnO2 or metallic MoO2 (rutile family, ~2-3% mismatch) as bottom-electrode template and 2-5% Al-doped TiO2 to raise the leakage barrier.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: doubling k from ZrO2's ~40 halves the 60-75:1 aspect ratio for the same Cs, and removes Zr/Hf ALD and ruthenium; Sn, Mo, Ti are diversified or US-sourced.

title: Catalyst-assisted wet etching digs 100:1 capacitor holes without fluorocarbon plasma
idea: Silicon dissolves only beneath a noble-metal catalyst in HF/H2O2 (metal-assisted chemical etching), so holes sink straight down at room temperature with no ion angular spread limiting depth. Pattern a catalyst mesh at storage-node pitch, sink 100:1 holes into silicon to revive trench-capacitor DRAM, then strip the catalyst in iodide etch.
why: Replaces the C4F6/C4F8 high-aspect-ratio plasma etch (PFAS-class gases, $10M+ tools, high energy) with a wet bench and pushes Cs past the 60-75:1 wall.

title: Chlorinated carborane photoacids replace perfluorinated sulfonates in DRAM resists
idea: A photoacid only needs a weakly coordinating conjugate base; the icosahedral carborane anion CB11H6Cl6- spreads its charge over 12 cage atoms, giving acid strength beyond triflic acid with zero C-F bonds. Pair it with triphenylsulfonium cations; the bulky cage also shortens acid diffusion for lower line-edge roughness.
why: Removes PFAS photoacid generators facing EU/US restriction from every ArF/EUV resist; boron is US-mined.

title: Self-passivated chamber walls eliminate NF3 cleans for ALD and CVD
idea: ALD/CVD films grow only where precursors find reactive sites; keep chamber walls and liners capped with a renewable small-molecule inhibitor re-dosed each lot and held above the precursor desorption temperature, so walls never accumulate film and periodic NF3 remote-plasma cleans disappear.
why: NF3 (GWP ~16,000) chamber cleaning is a top fab fluorochemical and greenhouse consumer; ~70-80% cut plus ~5-10% more tool uptime.

title: Gallium-free zinc-tin-silicon oxide channels for low-leak gain cells
idea: Oxide gain cells leak little because Eg>3 eV makes intrinsic carriers ~1e-25 cm-3 and holes immobile; mobility comes from overlapping metal ns orbitals, which Sn4+ 5s supplies as well as In3+, while Si (strong Si-O bond) takes Ga's carrier-suppressing role. Deposit amorphous Zn-Sn-Si-O by ALD as read and write channels.
why: Removes gallium (China ~98%, export-controlled) and indium from IGZO gain-cell roadmaps while keeping sub-aA off-current; Zn and Si are abundant and US-sourced.

title: Bonded 4H-SiC film access transistors erase the refresh leakage tail
idea: Generation leakage scales with intrinsic carrier density ni ~ exp(-Eg/2kT); 4H-SiC (3.26 eV) has ni ~1e-9 cm-3 versus 1e10 for Si, collapsing the 13 fA junction tail by many orders. Activate implants in a SiC wafer at 1600 C first, Smart-Cut a 100 nm film onto the DRAM wafer, and build access transistors in it under the capacitor process.
why: Fact 3: retention moves from 64 ms toward hours, deleting ~46 fJ/bit refresh and 10-20% bandwidth loss; SiC is Si+C and US-made. SiO2/SiC interface traps and mobility are the risk.

title: Anhydrous HF vapor and atomic hydrogen replace ultrapure-water cleans
idea: Clean targets are ~1e9-1e10 contaminant atoms/cm2, nanograms per wafer, yet each wafer consumes thousands of litres of UPW. Convert pre-deposition cleans to anhydrous HF/NH3 vapor oxide removal, remote atomic hydrogen for carbon and UV/O3 for organics, keeping one megasonic water rinse per module for particles.
why: Cuts UPW per wafer ~40-60% plus the energy of making it, and shrinks HF-laden wastewater.

title: Fab waste heat drives ceramic membrane distillation for zero discharge
idea: Separating pure water from brine has a thermodynamic minimum near 1 kWh/m3 while a fab rejects ~100 MW of 30-45 C process-cooling heat; use that temperature difference to drive vacuum membrane distillation of RO reject and CMP effluent through silane-hydrophobized alumina/SiC membranes instead of PTFE/PVDF.
why: Raises water recovery from ~60-70% to >95% on free heat, cutting withdrawal ~30-50% at drought-prone US sites with PFAS-free membranes.

title: Maskless interference lithography prints DRAM array lattices without EUV
idea: A cell array is a perfect 2D lattice whose information content is a few numbers, not a mask; three-beam 193 nm immersion interference writes the hexagonal hole lattice using ~100% of the photons, spacer pitch division shrinks it, and a relaxed DUV cut mask defines array edges.
why: Replaces 2-4 EUV array layers (single supplier, ~1 MW per scanner) with low-cost interference optics; array litho capex down ~5x.

title: Molten-salt electro-deoxidation turns quartz sand into silicon near thermodynamic minimum
idea: Reducing SiO2 to Si needs a minimum of ~9 kWh/kg while the Siemens chlorosilane route uses 50-100. Press SiO2 into cathodes, electro-deoxidize in molten CaCl2 at 850 C (FFC route), then reach 11N with a float-zone pass, skipping trichlorosilane, HCl and H2.
why: Polysilicon energy down ~4-5x and the chlorosilane chemical chain removed; reaching electronic-grade purity is the risk.

title: Molecular-monolayer doping replaces arsine, phosphine and ion implanters
idea: A junction needs ~1e13-1e15 dopant atoms/cm2, roughly one molecular monolayer; graft phosphonate or boronate monolayers from solution with dose set by ligand footprint, cap with oxide and spike-anneal. It is conformal, so it dopes 3D sidewalls that implanters cannot reach.
why: Removes toxic, concentrated dopant gases (AsH3, PH3, B2H6) and ~100+ kW implanters per tool, and enables doping of buried 3D tiers.

title: Stoichiometric-dose micro-gap ALD cuts zirconium and hafnium precursor tenfold
idea: A monolayer needs ~5e14 molecules/cm2, about 0.6 umol per 300 mm wafer per cycle, yet tools flow 20-50x that. Use a 0.2 mm-gap showerhead with stop-flow dose-and-hold exposure sized to the AR-squared Knudsen requirement of capacitor holes, so precursor dwells until consumed instead of streaming to the pump.
why: Precursor utilization rises from ~2-5% to ~30-40%: ~10x less Zr/Hf/Ti organometallic and abatement load per wafer.

title: Harvest DRAM dies from retired servers into CXL memory pools
idea: Charge storage causes no atomic change, so DRAM has no wear-out and a retired DIMM's dies still embody every scarce input. Desolder and retest dies at scale, rebin by speed and retention, and repackage them into CXL Type-3 expanders with stronger ECC and patrol scrub as tier-2 memory.
why: Adds ~10-20% of annual DRAM bit supply with zero new wafers, helium, quartz or tungsten, as a US remanufacturing business.

title: Thirty-two-cell local bitlines shrink the storage capacitor tenfold
idea: Signal is dV = Vcell*Cs/(Cs+CBL): a ~50 fF bitline forces ~5 fF cells, but a local two-transistor sense stage every 32 cells (CBL ~3 fF) yields the same ~100 mV from ~0.5 fF, so the capacitor becomes a shallow AR~7 cup.
why: Deletes the AR 60-75 mold etch (fluorocarbon gas, etch tools) and ~90% of ZrO2/TiN ALD material per bit, at the cost of more sense-amp area.

title: Fluoropolymer-free chemical and ultrapure-water wetted paths
idea: Wetted parts need only two properties, ppt-level metal extractables and chemical inertness; map each fluid to the cheapest material meeting both: PE/UHMWPE for UPW and HF, fused-silica- or sapphire-lined steel for hot sulfuric/peroxide, UPE filter membranes instead of PTFE, and CVD-SiC-coated valve seats.
why: Removes PFA/PTFE/PVDF (PFAS) from fab plumbing ahead of PFAS bans and fluoropolymer supplier exits, with equal or lower extractables.

title: Mine the fab's own WF6 exhaust as tungsten ore
idea: Tungsten CVD deposits only ~20-40% of delivered WF6, so scrubber streams carry W far richer than ore (~0.5% WO3). Trap exhaust in alkaline scrubbers as sodium tungstate, ion-exchange to ammonium paratungstate, calcine to WO3 and re-fluorinate with on-site F2 back to WF6.
why: Cuts new tungsten demand per wafer ~50-60% and turns the remainder into a US-domestic loop against China's ~80% share.

title: Shared energy-recovery free-electron laser feeds a whole EUV fab
idea: Tin-plasma EUV converts wall power at ~0.02%; an energy-recovery-linac FEL recycles the electron beam's energy and lases at 13.5 nm at ~0.1-1% wall-plug. One 10 kW source split by grazing-incidence optics feeds 10-20 scanners with no tin droplets and no hydrogen debris flow.
why: EUV electricity down ~5-10x and the tin-source/hydrogen chain removed, building on US national-lab accelerator expertise.

title: Metal-free vertical-bitline 3D gain-cell stack with doped-polysilicon wordline tiers
idea: Bits rise linearly with tiers while wafer cost rises ~1% per tier because lithography is shared. Stack 120 tiers of in-situ-doped poly-Si wordlines (no W replacement gate) with 2T0C Zn-Sn-O gain cells around vertical bitline holes in a relaxed ~100x100 nm per-tier footprint; gain cells tolerate poly resistance because their gate load is ~0.1 fF.
why: ~85 nm2/bit effective vs 864 nm2 today = ~10x density; ~20% added deposition/etch cost is offset by deleting 5-7 EUV layers; zero W, In or Ga.

title: Atmospheric spatial ALD deposits 150 oxide tiers without vacuum or helium
idea: Vacuum pumps, load locks and chambers dominate deposition cost, not atoms (a 10 nm tier is ~0.2 mg per wafer). Move wafers under gas-bearing spatial-ALD heads at 1 atm in N2, depositing ZnO channel, Al2O3 dielectric and Al:ZnO electrode tiers in-line at ~$3 per tier per wafer.
why: 150 tiers add ~$450 (~10%) to a ~$5k wafer for ~10x bits; no helium, no vacuum pumps, only abundant elements.

title: All-perovskite SrTiO3 capacitors on SrMoO3 electrodes shrink lateral 3D cells
idea: In 3D DRAM the lateral capacitor sets cell length and capacitance per area scales with k, so SrTiO3 (k~150-300) shortens it ~5x versus ZrO2. Use lattice-matched SrMoO3 (~1.8% mismatch, ~5 uOhm-cm, the most conductive oxide) for both electrodes, with an oxygen-getter interlayer to stop insulating SrMoO4 forming.
why: 5x shorter lateral cell x 40 tiers = ~10x density at equal tier cost; removes Hf, Zr, Ru and W from the capacitor using Sr, Ti and Mo.

title: Dopant-selective porous silicon replaces SiGe sacrificial layers in 3D DRAM
idea: SiGe/Si superlattices are strain-limited (mismatch accumulates, capping ~60-100 tiers) and need germanium. Grow a zero-mismatch superlattice of p+ (1e19 B) and lightly doped Si below 600 C, then anodize in HF: holes concentrate in p+ layers, turning only them into mesoporous Si (>100:1 selectivity), which is oxidized into inter-tier isolation.
why: No strain ceiling, so 200+ crystalline-Si tiers come from one epi run and one wet step: >=10x density at roughly today's wafer cost, with no germanium (China ~60%+).

title: Monolayer MoS2 channels collapse 3D tier pitch to twenty nanometers
idea: Tier pitch = channel + 2x dielectric + gate + isolation; a 0.65 nm MoS2 monolayer (Eg 1.8 eV, no dangling bonds, low off-leakage) replaces a 10-20 nm Si channel, shrinking tiers from ~50 to ~20 nm. Grow MoS2 per tier by low-temperature MOCVD.
why: A fixed 5 um etchable stack holds 250 tiers instead of 100; with a relaxed lateral cell that is ~10x density at the same etch/litho cost. Mo and S are US-abundant; W-based TMDs avoided.

title: Green-laser melt crystallizes each silicon tier using nine joules per wafer
idea: Melting a 20 nm Si film over a 300 mm wafer needs ~3 mg x ~2.8 MJ/kg = ~9 J, and a nanosecond pulse's ~100 nm thermal diffusion length keeps lower tiers cold. Deposit a-Si by PECVD and crystallize it with a green solid-state laser through grain-filter seed holes so each transistor sits in one grain; repeat for 32 tiers.
why: Crystalline-quality tiers at ~$15 per tier with no epi, no germanium and no neon excimer lasers; 32 tiers x relaxed cell = ~10x density at equal cost.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods use capacitorless 4F2 cells stacked eight high
idea: At 77 K subthreshold swing falls to ~15 mV/decade and thermally activated leakage drops >1e10, so a bare ~0.05 fF transistor gate holds charge for hours and needs no capacitor, while Cu/Mo wire resistivity drops ~6x. Build 4F2 vertical gain cells in 8 decks and run memory sleds immersed in LN2 made from air (no helium).
why: No capacitor + 8 decks = ~10x density at similar wafer cost; refresh vanishes and ~0.4 V operation cuts CV2 ~6x, offsetting cooling power at system level.

title: Vertical charge-coupled strings store 64 bits per pillar without capacitors
idea: A bit is just a charge packet and needs only a potential well, not a capacitor plus transistor. Use NAND-like vertical pillars whose tiered gates clock 3-phase wells that shift packets to one sense amplifier at the pillar top: 192 tiers give 64 bits per pillar at 60 nm pitch.
why: ~56 nm2/bit (~15x today) with one contact per 64 bits; deletes per-cell capacitor dielectric (Zr/Hf), tungsten contacts and EUV. Transfer inefficiency and serial latency are the risks.

title: Molybdenum polyoxometalate clusters store two quantized bits per node
idea: A 1 nm Keggin cluster [PMo12O40]3- accepts electrons in discrete redox steps ~0.2-0.4 V apart, so multilevel states are fixed by chemistry rather than by threshold variation. Graft a cluster monolayer as the floating storage node of a vertical gain cell, write levels with gate pulses and refresh like DRAM.
why: 2 bits per node, no capacitor, 4F2 vertical, 3 decks = ~10x density; Mo and P are abundant. Solid-state redox endurance is unproven.

title: Sodium-beta-alumina double-layer capacitors give 4x charge per area
idea: An electric double layer is a ~0.4 nm capacitor: ~20 uF/cm2 (~200 fF/um2) versus ~60 fF/um2 for ZrO2 stacks. A 5 nm Na-beta-alumina solid electrolyte (ionic conductor, electronic insulator) gives RC = (t/sigma*A)*C of ~1 ns for a 0.2 fF cell, and non-Faradaic charging causes no chemical wear.
why: 4x capacitance density makes 3D lateral capacitors 4x shorter; with 32 tiers that is ~10x density using Na, Al and O. Room-temperature ion response is the risk.

title: Reusable sapphire carriers let hot-grown memory stacks laser-lift onto CMOS
idea: Thermal budget, not physics, forbids crystalline oxides above CMOS. Grow the 100-tier array stack on a sapphire carrier at 700-900 C (crystalline STO/ZnO/Si tiers), bond it face-down onto the periphery wafer, release it by UV laser lift-off as in microLED, and re-polish the carrier for ~1000 uses.
why: Unlocks high-temperature tier materials for ~10x density via 100 tiers while substrate cost per wafer approaches zero and no second CZ wafer or quartz crucible is consumed.

title: Sugar-based block copolymers self-assemble 4.5-nanometer DRAM grids without EUV
idea: Self-assembly pitch is set by the Flory-Huggins parameter (chi*N >= 10.5); carbohydrate-polystyrene block copolymers have chi ~10x that of PS-b-PMMA, reaching ~9 nm pitch. Pattern a 4F2 vertical oxide-channel gain-cell array at F~4.5 nm (81 nm2/cell) with DUV chemical prepatterns guiding the assembly.
why: 81 vs 864 nm2 = ~10.7x density; replaces 5-7 EUV layers (single supplier, MW-class tools) with spin-coat and anneal using a bio-derived polymer. Defectivity is the risk.

title: Lattice-coded analog charge stores ten bits across three gain cells
idea: Thermal noise on a gain-cell node is sqrt(kT/C) ~2 mV against a ~1 V window, so Shannon allows ~8 bits per cell; drift and variation eat most of it, but coding 10 bits as one point in a 3-cell lattice (vector quantization, decoded at read) averages variation, and non-destructive reads allow verify-and-trim writes.
why: 3.3 bits/cell x 3 stacked oxide decks = ~10x bits per area at the same wafer cost; scarce material per bit falls ~10x.

title: Superconformal electroplated copper wordline tiers replace tungsten in 3D stacks
idea: Tungsten replacement gates in 3D stacks need ~25-30 nm tiers for acceptable resistance; Cu's resistivity is ~3x lower, so bottom-up electroplating with suppressor/accelerator additives fills ~12 nm tier cavities through the slit, using a ~1 nm self-forming MnSiO3 barrier.
why: Tier pitch down ~35%, so ~1.5x more tiers per etchable height; with a 120-tier gain-cell stack that is ~10x at equal cost, with no tungsten (China ~80%) or WF6.

title: Dopant-free Schottky tiers skip implant in buried 3D layers
idea: Implanters cannot reach buried tiers anyway, so remove dopants: use 6 nm undoped Si channels with nickel-silicide Schottky source/drain formed by lateral silicidation from the bitline hole, and set threshold by gate work function.
why: Thin dopant-free channels cut tier pitch to ~35 nm (150 tiers in 5 um, ~10x density) and remove arsine/phosphine and activation anneals. The Schottky leakage tail is the risk.

title: Ninety-degree hydrothermal zinc-oxide nanowires form vertical gain-cell forests
idea: Crystal growth needs supersaturation, not vacuum: ZnO nanowires grow from zinc nitrate/HMTA solution at 90 C on seed dots placed at 20 nm pitch by DUV plus pitch division. Each wire is a 4F2 vertical gain-cell channel; repeat seeding to build 5 decks.
why: 400 nm2/cell per deck x 5 decks = ~10x density with near-zero capex and energy for channel growth; Zn is abundant. Hydrogen-donor background doping (turn-off) is the risk.

title: Complementary SnO/ZnO sense amplifiers live inside the memory tiers
idea: Periphery is ~49% of the die because sense amps need CMOS on the substrate; p-type SnO (Sn2+ 5s hole band) plus n-type ZnO gives an oxide CMOS that deposits in the same tiers, so each tier carries its own sense/latch beside its cells.
why: Periphery falls from ~49% to ~10% with no separate CMOS wafer or bonding; with 60 tiers that is ~10x bits per die area at equal cost using Sn and Zn.

title: Sealed vacuum-gap bitlines let a quarter-sized capacitor suffice
idea: Bitline capacitance is mostly coupling through k~4-7 spacers; vacuum (k=1) gaps made by depositing a sacrificial carbon spacer, sealing it and ashing it out through a porous cap cut CBL ~3-4x, so the same signal needs ~1/4 the cell charge.
why: A quarter of Cs lets 3D lateral capacitors use plain Al2O3 (no Zr/Hf) at 1/4 the length; with 40 tiers that is ~10x density at equal cost. Air is the cheapest dielectric there is.

title: Mirror-polarity cells share every electrode between adjacent tiers
idea: A capacitor plate's field lines can terminate on both faces, yet stacked cells use only one; flip cell polarity on alternate tiers so one TiN/Mo plate serves the cells above and below as a common plate, deleting one metal layer per tier.
why: Tier height down ~30% and metal ALD per bit down ~50%: ~130 instead of 100 tiers per etchable height, which with a relaxed gain cell gives ~10x at equal cost.

title: One zinc-oxide film serves as channel, wordline and electrode via hydrogen
idea: ZnO conductivity spans ~1e-6 to 1e3 S/cm depending on hydrogen donors; deposit one ZnO film per tier and convert wordline/electrode regions into degenerate conductor with self-aligned H-plasma through the slit, leaving the masked channel semiconducting.
why: Each tier needs 2 depositions (ZnO + Al2O3) instead of ~4, cutting tier cost ~40% so 100+ tiers fit the same budget (~10x density) with no W, Mo, In or Ga. Hydrogen diffusion stability is the risk.

title: Zinc-oxide/cuprous-oxide diodes enable eight-deck selector-capacitor crosspoint DRAM
idea: Retention only needs reverse leakage below ~1e-4 A/cm2 at a 400 nm2 cell (Q~5e-16 C over 64 ms), within reach of wide-gap oxide heterojunctions. Stack a ZnO/Cu2O diode on a small MIM capacitor at each 4F2 crosspoint, deposited below 300 C, 8 decks high.
why: 4F2 x 8 decks = ~12x density with no per-cell transistor, using only Zn, Cu, Al and O. Forward current for 10 ns writes and half-select disturb are the risks.

title: Single carbon nanotubes coated as 1-micron coaxial storage capacitors
idea: Coaxial capacitance per length is 2*pi*eps/ln(r2/r1): a 1 nm-radius nanotube with 2 nm ZrO2 and a TiN shell gives ~2 fF/um, so a 1 um tube suffices at 10 nm pitch. Grow vertical tubes by methane CVD from Fe catalyst dots on each vertical-transistor drain.
why: ~100 nm2/cell vs 864 = ~9-10x density with an AR-100 pillar that is grown rather than etched (no fluorocarbon HAR etch), from carbon and iron. Catalyst contamination and tube placement are the risks.

title: Grayscale nanoimprint cuts the 3D staircase in one etch
idea: A staircase carries one piece of information, a depth profile, yet costs N resist-trim/etch cycles; imprint a single tapered resist profile from a grayscale NIL master and transfer it with one 1:1-selectivity etch, exposing every tier's landing pad at once.
why: Removes ~N/2 litho-etch cycles for 150+ tiers, so tier count can grow ~10x without added staircase cost, while cutting resist (PFAS PAG) and etch gas per bit.
